title: northstar-pocket-tactical-journal-izumi-tanaka
content:
One-line northstar: deliver consistent 99th percentile response time improvements for our most common 2–8 token prompts while keeping hosted cost/unit <= baseline.

Quarter goal (Q1 2025) — northstar-aligned sprint:
- Outcome: Reduce per-request tail latency by 15% for the small-text interactive workload and avoid >3% regression in generation quality.
- Why: user feedback + cost sensitivities from two customers; product needs predictable latency to enable realtime UX.

Key results (draft):
1) 99th percentile latency for interactive-2-8 tokens down from 210ms -> <=178ms on hosted by March 28.
2) Synthetic p95 throughput for default batch config >= 600 req/min on dedicated-minor cluster.
3) No more than 2 regressions flagged by eval harness vs baseline prompts.
4) Add one automated canary route in Redwood Console (simple rollout) and test with two internal apps.

Weekly ritual (what I actually do):
- Monday: quick metric snapshot, sanity-check dashboard, note anomalies.
- Wednesday: 30m experiment run + collect traces.
- Friday: write short retro (this doc), decide next micro-experiment.

Metric snapshot (week of 2025-02-10):
- interactive-2-8: p50 62ms, p95 120ms, p99 188ms (target p99 178ms) — small improvement since last week.
- error rate: 0.09% (ok).
- token cost/unit: 0.98x baseline (slightly better).

Current experiments (live):
A. kv-cache prefetch tweak (Kai): enable aggressive prefetch for repeated short prefixes. Running A/B on a 10% route. Hypothesis: reduce p99 by 6–10% for repeat customers. Data: early runs show p99 down 8% on stable traffic window.
B. kernel-selection policy (my spike): prefer fused-attn on Ampere if prompt len <= 12. TODO: coordinate with runtime team for rollback path.
C. batching debounce: reduce debounce to 8ms for low-latency tier — risk: throughput drop during spikes.

Observations / notes to self:
- Prefetch seems promising but trace shows occasional cache-miss spikes when prefix variability high. Need to add TTL smoothing.
- Kernel selection gives good upside but increases memory pressure; watch OOM signals on dedicated nodes.
- Debounce change reduced p50 but increased variance in tails on bursty weekdays. Might need dynamic debounce based on load signal.

Hypotheses for next sprint:
- H1: TTL smoothing + LRU cap will keep prefetch wins while eliminating cache churn -> net p99 improvement >=5%.
- H2: adaptive debounce (load-driven) will keep p50 benefits and prevent p99 regressions.

Failure modes / risks:
- Quality regression: quantization/kernel combo may alter logits subtly -> run eval harness per push.
- Customer impact: dedicated customers may see memory pressure; schedule a short maintenance window if rolling kernel changes.
- Observability gaps: need more KV-cache hit-rate per-token traces (file an observability ticket).

Open questions / unresolved:
- What is acceptable tail variance for Sales to sign off on SLA? (ask Samir this week)
- Do we have a simple rollback label for model variants in dedicated? If not, add to rollout checklist.

Actions (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] File lightweight observability ticket for per-token KV stats (me). Link: PROJ-4889.
- [ ] Add TTL smoothing to prefetch prototype and run 24h test (Kai + me).
- [ ] Draft canary run steps for kernel selection changes (include rollback + mem monitors).
- [ ] Sync with SRE on memory guardrails for Dedicated pools (Samir).
- [ ] Prep a 10-slide demo for internal infra sync showing before/after p99 impact.

Retro notes (quick hits):
- What worked: small scoped A/B gave usable signal quickly; pairing with Kai accelerated prototyping.
- What didn't: debounce tweak lacked golden signals to detect burstiness; should have simulated burst traffic first.
- Learnings: build small observability probes early (even if noisy) — they pay off.

Template bits to copy into future weeks:
- metric snapshot table (p50/p95/p99, cost ratio, error rate)
- experiment card (owner, hypothesis, metric, rollout %, notes)
- failure-mode checklist (quality, infra, customer impact, observability)

Quick links and references:
- eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/342
- related confluence note: https://redwood-confluence.company/display/ENG/Latency+Playbook
- jira: PROJ-4823 (kernel selection spike), PROJ-4889 (observability probe)

Notes to future self:
- If a change improves p50 at cost of p99, stop and re-evaluate. Tail > top-line.
- Keep experiments <= 2 concurrent; I've burned time juggling 4 before.

End-of-week micro-retro (2025-02-14):
- Feeling: optimistic but cautious. Prioritize stability + small wins.
- Next week's focus: TTL smoothing + mem guardrails.

-- scratch area (raw quick notes):
- "prefix = user:quick-command" seems to dominate 12% of traffic; worth dedicated micro-cache?
- call with SRE Thu 9am.
- chart to add: p99 by client id (top 20 clients)
- remove optimistic debug logs before canary (noise concerns)
